rule_text: The Control Room Operator (CRO) is responsible for monitoring all process parameters, initiating control actions, and logging data.
The Field Operator is responsible for physical rounds, sampling, and verification of local gauge readings.
The Shift Supervisor has authority to approve deviations from normal operating targets and to authorise interlock bypasses.
Any condition not met must be reported to the Shift Supervisor.
All safety interlocks tested and enabled with no active trips.
Sulfur melter S-101 temperature ≥ 135°C.
Acid circulation pump P-107A available and seal flush water flowing.
Start acid circulation pump P-107A and establish a flow rate of at least 600 m³/h through the absorption tower.
Initiate combustion air blower B-103 and adjust air flow to 12,000 Nm³/h.
Light sulfur burner F-102 and increase sulfur feed at a rate not exceeding 50 kg/h per minute until reaching 2000 kg/h.
When converter Bed 1 inlet temperature exceeds 400°C, slowly raise sulfur feed to normal range while adjusting air flow to maintain SO2 concentration at 10.0–10.5% vol.
Maintain 3800–4200 kg/h
Low alarm at 3500 kg/h
High alarm at 4500 kg/h
Trip at 4700 kg/h: close sulfur feed valve XV-101 and initiate automatic water wash of burner.
Maintain 580–610°C
Low alarm at 550°C
High alarm at 615°C
Trip at 620°C: open converter bypass damper DV-201 and initiate emergency cooling.
Maintain 98.3–98.7% H₂SO₄
Low alarm at 98.0%
High alarm at 99.0%
Trip at 97.5% or 99.2%: close acid product valve and divert to spill tank.
Interlock bypass for any trip function requires written authorisation from the Shift Supervisor and must be recorded in the bypass log.
The Burner Management System (BMS) logic performs a pre-purge of the combustion chamber for 60 seconds before allowing ignition.
All safety interlocks shall be tested every 6 months.
In the event of a loss of instrument air, the fail-safe valves shall move to their safe positions as specified in P&ID 02-01.
The outgoing CRO shall complete the Shift Handover Log (form OP-LOG-001) and verbally brief the incoming CRO on current operating status, alarms, and maintenance activities.
The process log shall be updated every 30 minutes with: SO2 feed rate, Bed 1 outlet temperature, acid concentration, and any alarm occurrences.
The Field Operator shall measure absorption acid concentration every 2 hours using the hydrometer and record the value in the log.
The online SO2 analyzer AI-201 shall be calibrated every 7 days by the Instrument Technician using certified 10.0% SO₂ span gas.
The differential pressure across Bed 1 (ΔP-201) shall be recorded once per shift. If ΔP exceeds 150 mbar, the Shift Supervisor shall be notified.
Bed 1 catalyst shall be replaced after 30,000 cumulative operating hours or if ΔP persists above 150 mbar after screening.
The CRO shall immediately execute the actions listed for each trip scenario.
The Field Operator shall confirm valve positions physically within 10 minutes of a trip.
TI-202 ≥ 620°C (2oo3 voting)
Open converter bypass damper DV-201; start emergency quench air injection
Confirm DV-201 open and quench air flowing; reduce sulfur feed to zero if not already tripped
1 minute
Stop acid pump P-107; close acid valve XV-301
Verify pump stopped and valve closed; check pump mechanical seal
2 minutes
AI-301 ≥ 50 ppm SO₂
Initiate stack emergency scrubber; trip sulfur feed
Evacuate downwind area; sound site alarm; notify Environmental Manager
1 minute
Pressure switch PS-501 ≤ 4.0 bar
All control valves fail to safe position per P&ID
Verify valve positions; shut down plant manually if needed
5 minutes
All trip events shall be logged in the Trip Log (LOG-ESD-001) within 15 minutes of occurrence.
Reduce sulfur feed to zero at a rate not exceeding 100 kg/h per minute.
Stop combustion air blower after burner temperature drops below 300°C.
Continue acid circulation for at least 30 minutes to cool the converter.
Close all acid transfer valves to storage.
If a spill is detected, the Field Operator shall immediately isolate the source and activate the containment sump pump.
Prior to any maintenance work, the equipment must be isolated from all hazardous energy sources and locked out in accordance with Apex LOTO Standard STD-SAF-012.
The Maintenance Supervisor shall verify zero energy state and issue a safety work permit before work commences.
Inspect and grease bearings and check seal integrity every 2,000 operating hours; performed by Maintenance Technician.
Perform vibration analysis and bearing temperature check, replace oil every 4,000 operating hours; performed by Condition Monitoring Technician.
Overhaul (replace mechanical seal, impeller wear rings) every 8,000 operating hours or 12 months, whichever first; performed by Maintenance Fitter.
Internal inspection and catalyst sampling every 4 years; performed by Inspection Engineer.
Check packing and acid distributor, clean every 2 years; performed by Process Engineer.
Calibrate every 7 days using span gas at 10.0% SO₂; performed by Instrument Technician.
Calibrate every 3 months by 3-point check vs certified RTD; performed by Instrument Technician.
Calibrate every 6 months using deadweight tester; performed by Instrument Technician.

rule_text: Verify calibration every 6 months by clamp-on ultrasonic method; performed by Instrument Technician.
All hot work within 15 m of the sulfur melter requires a hot work permit and continuous gas monitoring for SO₂ and H₂S.
Confined space entry into the converter vessel or absorption tower requires a confined space permit, atmospheric testing, and a standby person.
